title: 2010 AMC 8 Problem 13
statement: The lengths of the sides of a triangle in inches are three consecutive integers. The length of the shortest side is \(30\%\) of the perimeter. What is the length of the longest side?

solutions.text:
Let \(s\) be the smallest length. Then, all the side lengths are \(s,\) \(s+1,\) \(s+2.\) This would make the perimeter equal to \(3s+3.\) Since \(s = 0.3(3s+3),\) then \(s = 0.9s + 0.9 .\) This makes \(0.1s = 0.9,\) so \(s = 9\) which makes the longest side length \(s + 2 = 11.\)

Thus, the answer is E .
hints: Use the condition that the shortest side is \(30\%\) of the perimeter.
Let the side lengths be three consecutive integers starting with the shortest.
